# MacBook Pro display review

The display is central to the laptop experience. We tested the screen with everyday applications, full-screen video, and games to understand how the new cutout affects the interface. The following photographs show where the menu bar sits and how full-screen applications use the available space.

[![](https://cdn.arstechnica.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/MacBook-Pro-Dynamic-Island-1024x466.jpg)](https://cdn.arstechnica.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/MacBook-Pro-Dynamic-Island.jpg)

The Dynamic Island on the MacBook Pro. Samuel Axon

[![The Music app full-screen with a black bar along the top](https://cdn.arstechnica.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/MacBook-Pro-fullscreen-1024x415.jpg)](https://cdn.arstechnica.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/MacBook-Pro-fullscreen.jpg)

Full-screen apps cut off just below the Dynamic Island by default, just like with the notch before. Samuel Axon
